ground_truth.description: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.root_cause: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet with static signature bound to entrypoint. Attempt validateUserOp → reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller. PoC: Add test to test/modules/ERC4337v07.t.sol: test_validateUserOp_staticSig_callerMismatch_reverts. Uses server and forge test.
ground_truth.fix_description: Avoid external self-call; propagate intended caller into validation.

vulnerabilities.explanation: validateUserOp performs an external self-call `this.isValidSignature(...)` (line 36). This changes msg.sender from entrypoint to the wallet contract itself. BaseAuth.signatureValidation (called via isValidSignature) enforces static signature caller binding with `if (addr != address(0) && addr != msg.sender) revert InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller`. Static signatures explicitly bound to the entrypoint therefore always revert.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario:
1. User creates static signature bound to entrypoint address via setStaticSignature.
2. User submits UserOperation through ERC-4337 entrypoint.
3. validateUserOp executes the external isValidSignature call.
4. signatureValidation sees msg.sender == wallet (not entrypoint) and reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller.
5. UserOperation validation fails permanently for any static-signature user.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Replace the external self-call with an internal call: `if (!isValidSignature(userOpHash, userOp.signature)) return SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED;` or propagate the intended caller (entrypoint) into signatureValidation so static-signature checks use the original caller.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a DoS vulnerability affecting ERC-4337 static signatures. The external self-call in validateUserOp breaks the caller-binding check in BaseAuth, causing all static signatures bound to the entrypoint to fail validation. This is a concrete, exploitable issue matching the provided benchmark description.
